Welcome! This site collects notes and computational notebooks for social media research, developed through my [research and teaching at the Media Informatics Group, University of Regensburg](https://go.ur.de/michael-achmann).

## Research Seminar · Winter 2026/27

This semester, **Computational Analysis of Visual Social Media** focuses on framing analysis of political TikTok content with possible AI components. We collect and prepare video material, develop a coding framework from literature and the data, and create independent human annotations. Teams then compare vision-language models or input representations against a shared reference dataset.

[View the course plan and requirements](getting-started/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

### Semester at a Glance

| Phase | What we work on |
|-------|-----------------|
| Foundations | Social media analysis, framing, AI, and political content |
| Collection and preparation | A shared TikTok corpus, preprocessing, and video material |
| Framework and annotation | Inductive coding, a literature-based codebook, pilot rounds, and independent annotations |
| Team experiments and evaluation | Model and input comparisons, agreement, error analysis, and peer feedback |

The [full schedule](getting-started/index.qmd#course-schedule) lists the Monday sessions from 12 October 2026 to 1 February 2027. It is our working plan; check GRIPS for announcements, formal requirements, and the final submission deadline.

## Materials and Update Status

The course material is being revised for winter 2026/27. **Status below: 2 November 2026.** A revised page may still contain historical notebooks; follow the notes on each page before running code.

| Material | Status and next steps |
|----------|-----------------------|
| [Course organisation](getting-started/index.qmd) | **Updated:** this semester's focus, schedule, and report guidance. Formal requirements and deadlines remain subject to confirmation in GRIPS. |
| [TikTok collection](data-collection/tiktok.qmd) | **New guide:** collecting media and metadata with Tidal Tales, with an alternative collection workflow and sampling limitations. |
| [Agreement and evaluation](evaluation/agreement.qmd) | **Revised:** checked interactive examples, nominal agreement, binary and macro F1, and a prominently linked evaluation notebook. |
| [Data preparation](processing/preprocessing.qmd) | **In revision:** importing current exports and preparing image and video observations. Older OCR and transcription examples remain available. |
| [Tools](basics/tools.qmd) and [API basics](basics/openai.qmd) | **Needs an update:** tool setup, screenshots, and API examples. |
| [Text exploration](processing/exploration.qmd) and [classification](processing/classification.qmd) | **Needs an update:** model-specific examples, structured outputs, and reproducible workflows. Link repairs alone do not validate the older code. |
| [Visual exploration](image-analysis/exploration.qmd) and [classification](image-analysis/classification.qmd) | **Needs a review:** methods, model examples, and their fit with this semester's video-framing questions. |
| [Reporting](reporting/index.qmd) | **Existing material:** statistical analysis and visualisation examples; notebook content still needs review. |

### Foundations and Further Material

- [Interdisciplinary approaches](getting-started/theory.qmd) and [related work](getting-started/related-work.qmd): theoretical perspectives and guidance for literature reviews. The literature coverage needs a refresh.
- [Data collection in a post-API world](data-collection/index.qmd): conceptual, ethical, and legal considerations. Check current access conditions before choosing a collection method.
- [Instagram posts](data-collection/ig-posts.qmd) and [stories](data-collection/ig-stories.qmd): existing workflows and explicitly marked historical approaches. Their current tool compatibility still needs review.
- [Text as data and data organisation](processing/index.qmd) and [images as data](image-analysis/index.qmd): foundations for preparing and interpreting computational observations.
- [Human annotations](evaluation/index.qmd) and [image annotations](evaluation/label-studio-images.qmd): coding instructions and Label Studio examples.
- [Fine-tuning BERT](processing/bert_classification.ipynb): an earlier notebook for binary text classification, to be reviewed before reuse.
- [GPT literature assistant](notebooks/literature-review-v2.ipynb): an archived API example, retained for reference.
- [Student projects](projects/index.qmd): examples from earlier course iterations.
